candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — MDRO / Contact Precautions / draining wound
candidate.educational_objective: Apply Contact Precautions in addition to Standard Precautions for an acute-care client with a target MDRO and uncontained draining wound.

options.D: Standard Precautions only, with no additional transmission-based precautions

candidate.rationale: CDC recommends Standard Precautions for all patient encounters and, in acute-care hospitals, routine Contact Precautions for patients infected or colonized with target MDROs. Contact Precautions also apply when excessive or uncontained wound drainage increases environmental contamination and transmission risk. Therefore A is the best answer. Airborne or Droplet Precautions are not indicated solely by the scenario described.
candidate.source_claim_supported: In acute care, target-MDRO infection warrants Contact Precautions in addition to Standard Precautions; uncontained/excessive wound drainage independently supports Contact Precautions because of transmission risk.

candidate.stem: In an acute-care hospital, a client has an infected wound with a target multidrug-resistant organism (MDRO) and drainage that is not fully contained by the dressing. Which precautions should the nurse implement?
